blockers.title: The file-backed manifest join accepts bytes from the wrong member of the authenticated package
evidence: authenticatedManifest members contain both relativePath and sha256, but the only normative join compares openedBytesSha256 with exactly one manifest sha256. No rule compares openedObjectObservation.canonicalPath, an install-root-relative derivation of that path, or the signed origin to the matched member.relativePath.
The manifest uniqueness rule only prevents duplicate hashes or paths. It guarantees that a hash selects one member, not that it selects the member installed at the opened path.

A concrete counterexample satisfies every stated check: an authenticated package contains regular files A and B with unique hashes hA and hB; after installation, copy B's bytes over A without changing package ownership metadata; resolve A; retain canonicalPath A and openedBytesSha256 hB. The package trust result and signed {name, version, digest} remain valid, and hB matches exactly one authenticated manifest member, so v22 accepts B at A.
INSTALL-ROOT-VOLUME does not sign a canonical object path, and EXTERNAL-ORIGIN signs A while the attack keeps A. Neither origin rule supplies the missing equality to manifest relativePath.

identityRuleShape defines any authenticity evidence mismatch as drift and NT-TCB-3 requires drift to refuse. The hash-only join instead treats every unique regular-file member of one package as interchangeable at every owned path.
blockers.impact: A loader, framework, libc, or comparable PLATFORM-ATTESTED object can be replaced with a different member from the same authenticated package and still be admitted. This is a reproducible false allow in mandatory Linux taxonomy cells, so G22 cannot establish the required identity-drift property.
blockers.requiredRepair: Derive exactly one package-relative path from the same-event canonical opened path under a named install root and normalization grammar. Require that path and openedBytesSha256 both equal the same authenticatedManifest member. Bind the retained member, package payload digest, and event association token together; reject traversal, root ambiguity, missing members, duplicate paths, and any hash-only match to a different member.

blockers.title: NT_GNU_BUILD_ID equality is not a cryptographic measurement of the executing kernel bytes
evidence: v22 correctly retires the /boot filename and osrelease suffix as an authenticity bind, then reads an NT_GNU_BUILD_ID descriptor from /sys/kernel/notes and compares that token with a note in one authenticated package member.

The contract names no algorithm that derives the descriptor from all executing kernel bytes, no recomputation over those bytes, no measured-boot or runtime measurement root, and no platform trust decision covering the executing image. It merely compares two embedded identifiers.

A different or modified kernel can retain or copy the authenticated member's NT_GNU_BUILD_ID note. The package payload and package trust result remain authentic, /sys/kernel/notes returns the copied descriptor, exactly one package member contains it, and executingKernelBind passes while the executing code is different.

The uniqueness rule within one payload does not supply collision resistance or byte coverage. It excludes two package members sharing a token but does not exclude an unauthenticated executing kernel sharing that token.

The v21 required repair called for an observation cryptographically bound to the executing kernel/ABI subject. Replacing a filename token with another unauthenticated token does not provide that property.
blockers.impact: A substituted Linux kernel can satisfy the signed package identity and pathless bind without its executing bytes matching the authenticated payload. OS ABI is mandatory and forced through PATHLESS-PLATFORM-ATTESTED, so the core platform identity can false-allow drift.
blockers.requiredRepair: Use a trusted cryptographic measurement of the executing kernel bytes or immutable loaded image, with a named algorithm and coverage, and bind that measurement through a verified boot/measurement trust result to the exact authenticated package member digest. If the executing bytes cannot be measured or attested, refuse or remove the profile; an embedded build-id alone must not establish authenticity.

shouldFix.title: The new authenticity-bind evidence is not a closed OS-discriminated retained record
evidence: objectAuthenticityBind.retained requires file-backed events to retain openedObjectObservation and the matching manifest member {relativePath, sha256}. retainedEventSchema names only the closed openedObjectObservation {canonicalPath, openedBytesSha256, associationToken}; it has no matching-manifest-member field, and extras rejection prevents nesting that member there.
authenticatedManifest occurs only as the operation's schema definition. No producer-visible retained event field binds the selected member to the package core, trust decision, or event token.

executingKernelBind is described as a closed {executingKernelBuildId, authenticatedKernelMember} event field, but authenticatedKernelMember has no closed retained value shape, canonical member identity, package digest field, or encoding.

openedObjectObservation is unconditionally required on every file-backed PLATFORM-ATTESTED event in retainedEventSchema and both file-backed laterEventVariant objects, including macos/codesign. objectAuthenticityBind.fileBacked supplies only rpm and deb authenticatedManifest sources, while fileBackedBinding says macOS uses the SecCode guest instead. One rule requires Linux-style hash evidence on macOS and another replaces it with codesign.
These are live schema rules, not historical text. A producer cannot know whether to emit a manifest member, where to emit it, or whether macOS must participate in the package-manifest join.
shouldFix.impact: The intended live comparisons are visible, but retained qualification evidence and mandatory macOS file-backed records are not represented by one closed union. Implementations can emit different event shapes or be unable to audit the claimed object-to-manifest equality.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Define an OS/scheme-discriminated closed objectAuthenticityBind record. For Linux file-backed events include openedObjectObservation plus the exact matchedManifestMember and authenticated package-payload identity in one retained event field. Define a closed authenticatedKernelMember shape for Linux pathless. For macOS, require only the same SecCode guest bind and explicitly forbid Linux package-manifest fields.

shouldFix.title: The Linux package-payload source still contains the prohibited or-choice and no reproducible archive acquisition
evidence: v22 claims there is no or-choice file input, but rpm-checksig.checksigArgv is unchanged and still passes the literal alternative <NEVRA-or-installed-package>. No rule selects one grammar or names an exact RPM payload path/handle.

authenticatedManifest.sourceRpm requires extracting the authenticated rpm payload after checksig success, yet the operation never binds the checked payload bytes or their header/package digest to authenticityCore.payload.digest. The rpmdb ownership and SHA256HEADER queries do not name the archive from which extraction occurs.

The rpm interface remains explicitly unpinned across major versions and parses a human stdout token without a locale or exact byte normalization. The same profile can therefore depend on ambient command version and localization.

The apt branch identifies a trusted index SHA256 but names no exact acquisition of the corresponding .deb, no retained Release/Packages identity, and no explicit equality between the acquired archive's computed SHA-256 and the index/core digest before data.tar extraction.
These gaps also leave the generic authenticityCore.packageBytes rule and the concrete manifest source without one executable chain from authenticated archive bytes to the retained member.
shouldFix.impact: Even after the two false-allow blockers are repaired, implementations can choose different RPM inputs or package archives and derive different manifests for the same profile. Some environments can only invent an archive source or refuse, so the operation is not reproducible.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Replace the RPM placeholder with one exact archive-byte source and argument grammar; bind its computed digest/header identity to the signed core before signature verification and extraction. Pin or normalize the interface and output bytes. For apt, name the exact trusted Release/Packages object, acquire one .deb, compute and compare its SHA-256 to the authenticated index/core value, and retain those identities before extracting the manifest.
